findings.title: Embedded sections are not byte-identical to the manifested files
findings.criterion_ref: PKGV2-T10 — the live originals are said to be “proven byte-identical in manifest.v1.json beside the bundle.”
findings.trigger: A reviewer or downstream process extracts any fenced section as the source text and recomputes its SHA-256.
findings.consequence: Every embedded file fails its manifested digest. In particular, the embedded graph does not match the digest approved by contract v3, so the bundle cannot serve as the claimed frozen, byte-identical reviewed logic.
findings.evidence: Each of the ten sections contains an extra blank line immediately before its closing fence. The embedded implementation.graph.v6.yaml is 27,476 bytes with SHA-256 c0e320e7ead061dc18cb0d01c3ca68cd2706f444694d10d7ce5cc42a1d353ae5, while the live and manifested file is 27,475 bytes with SHA-256 b186b58828fd1f490a57dd3cfe7d26bcdff70a37f78d6d996f2f8234ef2b5c26. Removing exactly the final extra LF restores the manifest hash for all ten embedded sections.

findings.title: The suite does not assert that N20’s real scan passes with zero violations
findings.criterion_ref: PKGV2-T22(a) — dedicated tests must prove N20’s real node-scoped command “now passes with zero violations.”
findings.trigger: The N20 scanner regresses to return a nonzero exit status or violations while continuing to report the expected scanned-file scope.
findings.consequence: The relevant tests can remain green even though the exact N20 scan is blocked again, so the required behavioral regression proof is absent.
findings.evidence: In tests/test_execution_package_v2.py, test_n20_node_mode_includes_its_newly_owned_egress_module_and_test (bundle lines 1692–1700) calls the real command but only checks two scanned-file memberships; it never asserts code == 0, payload['valid'], or an empty violations list. test_node_scoped_scan_covers_exactly_its_own_migration_owned_test_files (lines 3115–3130) likewise checks only scope. The run() helper returns nonzero status without raising.

observations: The live plan validator returned valid: true, and the exact live N20 command currently returned success with zero violations; RC6-QA-002 concerns the missing automated assertion, not the present scan result.
Pytest collected exactly 160 tests. Full execution was unavailable in the read-only QA sandbox because pytest could not create a temporary directory.
The graph’s 17-file scan scope, excluded Gemini-pipeline files, parent collect_files behavior, deprecated-v5 digest, and N20-recorded production hashes otherwise matched the stated correction.

validate_spec_approval_contract() still has a stale schema-v2/contract-v2 docstring even though its constants and behavior correctly bind schema v3 and contract v3; this does not defeat a numbered criterion.
reasoning: The central scan-scope correction behaves correctly in direct read-only checks, and I found no basis to reject the deliberate rc3 approval-manifest retention or the v5-to-v6 graph changes. However, the bundle’s systematic extra LF defeats its claimed byte identity, and the suite omits the explicit N20 zero-violation assertion required by PKGV2-T22(a). Both survive scrutiny at or above the major threshold.
